takeaway: A painless, soft lump below the ear lobule, with bilateral parotid lumps and an intact facial nerve in an older patient, is a Warthin tumour (adenolymphoma).

question.text: An 83-year-old woman has a soft, painless 1 cm lump below the left ear lobule, a similar lump on the other side, and no facial nerve involvement. Most likely diagnosis?
question.say: An 83-year-old woman has a soft, painless one centimetre lump below the left ear lobule, a similar lump on the other side, and no facial nerve involvement. What is the most likely diagnosis?

lines.text: An older woman has a soft, painless lump just below the ear lobule, and a similar lump on the other side.
That position is the parotid gland, and bilateral lumps are the clue.
Most parotid tumours are pleomorphic adenomas, and monomorphic adenomas make up the rest.
The commonest monomorphic adenoma is the Warthin tumour, which is an adenolymphoma.
Warthin tumours are more commonly bilateral, just like this patient.
The facial nerve is intact, and weakness would suggest malignant infiltration, so this is benign.
